content:
maria: heads-up: we're seeing a correlated bump in preemptible interrupts in us-west1 starting ~11:40 UTC, impacting a few Dedicated pools. Noticed a 3x spike in reclaim events and a subtle tail latency increase on rl-infer routes.
lee(oncall): on it. can you paste the dashboard link?
maria: https://grafana.redwood/team/infra/d/spot-health/spot-availability?orgId=1&from=now-1h&to=now  - look at panel 'reclaims by zone' and '95th latency by route' (rl-infer-prod).
dmitri: I just checked node autoscaler logs, there are a bunch of `InstancePreempted` events. kubectl shows mixed-capacity pools (preemptible + on-demand) but the fallback ratio is low because our scheduling prefers preemptible for cost.
sara: can we throttle new batch jobs onto preemptible-only pools until we confirm stable capacity?
maria: yes, suggested immediate mitigation: 1) disable preemptible placement for new rollout tasks 2) increase on-demand buffer to 10% of capacity 3) trigger a temporary routing policy to prefer dedicated-on-demand for rl-infer-prod.
lee(oncall): implementing mitigation 1 and 2 now. running: `kubectl label node -l pool=rl-infer preemptible=false --overwrite` on the canary subset and bumping cluster-autoscaler minOnDemandNodes.
ops-bot: deploy started by lee(oncall) for label change - job id 4521 - ETA 2m
dmitri: for longer term, we should have an alert that correlates rise in `spot_reclaims_total` with increased 95th latency for critical routes. Right now we alert on raw reclaim counts but it's noisy.
sara: agree. propose a composite alert: when (reclaim_rate_zone > 0.5 per minute AND increase_in_route_95p > 20% over baseline) for 10m -> P1. Otherwise (reclaim_rate_zone > 2/min sustained 30m) -> P2.
maria: validation: baseline calc should be rolling 7-day median by zone and by pool type. we had a false alarm last month because single-day baseline was low.
dmitri: sample PromQL for reclaim rate by zone: ```
sum by(zone)(rate(spot_reclaims_total[5m]))
```
and for percent change in 95p latency: ```
(quantile_over_time(0.95, http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="rl-infer-prod"}[1h]) - scalar(hourly_baseline_95p)) / scalar(hourly_baseline_95p)
```
maria: hourly_baseline_95p would be computed offline as a timeseries with `record:` rule. dmitri can help with the recording rule.
dmitri: I'll add a recording rule `hourly_baseline_95p{route=~".*"}` computed as `avg_over_time(quantile_over_time(0.95, http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[1h])[7d:1h])` — we need to be careful with ranges in PromQL but conceptually that's it.
sara: aside: we should also monitor the pool fill ratio where `preemptible_fill = preemptible_allocated / preemptible_capacity` because sudden drop indicates mass reclaiming. add a panel and a 15m alert if `preemptible_fill < 0.3` AND reclaim_rate > 1/min.
maria: good call. also track `reclaim_latency_ms` distribution to detect if reclaims are concentrated at particular times (provider maintenance windows).
lee(oncall): quick operational checks I ran: `kubectl get nodes -l preemptible=true -o wide` shows many nodes in NotReady shortly after reclaims. I also saw GCE metadata messages `Instance terminated by maintenance`.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-054 - Preliminary: spot availability spike in us-west1 - assigned to eng-infra
maria: cost note - if we increase on-demand buffer to 10% cluster-wide for a month, rough delta is +8% on GPU spend. still cheaper than 20% SLA violations we've been seeing.
dmitri: for mixed-pool scheduling improvement, we can change node affinity weights so latency-sensitive routes prefer on-demand by default, but allow best-effort jobs to use preemptible aggressively. This needs config change in our scheduler plugin.
sara: plan: short-term mitigations applied; mid-term: implement composite alert + baseline recording rules + dashboard panels (reclaims by zone, preemptible_fill, route_95p_delta, reclaim_latency_hist); long-term: scheduler affinity changes + autoscaler policy to maintain on-demand buffer per region.
lee(oncall): i pushed the label change and increased autoscaler min-demand nodes. monitoring for 30m.
maria: thx. can someone own the alert doc and a runbook update? I can draft the runbook but need an owner for the alert rule and Grafana panels.
dmitri: i'll own the Prometheus recording rules and alert PR.
sara: i'll own the Grafana panels and runbook edit.
lee(oncall): I’ll monitor the oncall channel and escalate if latency creeps back up.
maria: appreciate it. follow-up: let's add synthetic checks that simulate short-lived heavy prefixes to test cache/kv pressure under reclaim scenarios.
dmitri: noted. adding to infra backlog.
ops-bot: incident INC-2026-054 updated: mitigations applied - on-demand buffer increased, scheduling label adjusted - status: monitoring
sara: reminder: add a playbook entry to run `kubectl cordon` + `drain` strategy for partially preempted nodes to reduce pod churn. include sample commands in runbook.
maria: example commands for runbook: ```
kubectl cordon <node>
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
```
lee(oncall): all good for now. keeping this thread open for 30m to confirm stability.
